checker_history.note: corrected contract shipped 2026-11-10 without touching any vendored byte. The vendored `LetterFrequencyChecker.build_description` replaces a `letter` kwarg outside a-z with `random.choice(string.ascii_letters)`, so the two pinned cells whose ask is punctuation (`ifeval-1122` = '#', `ifeval-1129` = '!') were decided by a coin flip under `pub-ifeval-v1` (measured strict pass 4/12 and 7/12 over 12 draws of byte-identical shipped answers). v2 restores the pinned literal character on the built instruction and counts it as-is; it re-asserts the five SHA-1/16 vendored pins above on every run and refuses to score if they move, pins determinism (20 identical draws per affected cell), and fails closed if v1 and v2 differ on more than those 2 cells. All five published IFEval arms were rescored from the shipped answer bytes (three independent scorer passes each); the per-arm corrections, the recomputed paired tests and the residual langdetect band are in IFEVAL-RESULT.md. The published `pub-ifeval-v1` rows and verdict files stay published unchanged.

pin_history.note: bytes of `pub-ifeval-v2` as published on 2026-11-10 at 04:33 UTC. The pin-audit commit renamed the module's hash helpers (`sha1_16` / `sha256_16` / `tasks_sha256_16`) and routed the digest tasks cell through `pub_bench_score.manifest_tasks_cell`; no scoring path, checker call or rounding changed. Proof, run after the edit with zero model calls: all three re-scorable IFEval arms re-scored from the shipped answer bytes gave the same totals as before the edit — bare 469, `pub-repair-v1` 497, `pub-repair-v2` 510 of 541 strict under `pub-ifeval-v2` — and the scorer self-test stayed 22/22. Documents citing the old value (`IFEVAL-RESULT.md`, `PUB-PLAN.md`) refer to the run made against those bytes and stay true of that run.

ifeval.hash_note: IFEval is the one set whose published tasks pin is SHA-1/16: `scripts/pub_bench_ifeval.py` hashed the tasks file with SHA-1 before any other set existed, and every published ifeval digest row prints that value. The SHA-256/16 of the identical 541 rows is labelled `tasks_sha256_16`, so an outside check with `sha256sum benchmarks/public/ifeval.tasks.jsonl | cut -c1-16` resolves to it instead of looking like a moved task file. Nothing was re-measured by this label: the task file, the verdict files and the digest rows are byte-unchanged. `scripts/pub_bench_score.manifest_tasks_cell` now reads this pin instead of re-hashing, and refuses to write a digest cell for a file that matches neither label. Convention of this entry's tool pins (pin audit 2026-11-10): the published `checker_files` values and `reference_response_file.sha16` are SHA-1/16 (that is what the scorer re-asserts at run time), so the `*_sha256_16` twins added here are what `sha256sum <file> | cut -c1-16` gives. Both name identical bytes; neither pin was re-minted.

The tracked tasks file carries, per question, the public tests plus hidden_count and the SHA-256/16 of the canonical hidden-test JSON, and `score` fail-closes if a sidecar row does not match that pin. Publishing this payload as a GitHub release asset is a separate owner decision; until then the payload lives only on the local box and an outside reader can verify the per-question pins but not re-run the hidden battery.

hash_conventions: Two hash conventions appear in this repo and they are not interchangeable. `tasks_sha16`/`raw_sha16`/`sha16` in a digest row or in `checker_files` is SHA-256/16 (`sha256sum F | cut -c1-16`) for every set EXCEPT ifeval, whose published tasks pin is SHA-1/16 and is labelled here with `tasks_sha1_16` + `tasks_sha256_16` + `hash_note`. `scripts/security/secret_scan.py` binds its byte-pinned exceptions with SHA-1/16. The file index in `benchmarks/public/arms/README.md` pins BOTH conventions per row and `scripts/pub_arms_index.py --check` fails closed if a sidecar stops carrying SHA-256/16 of its target. Tool and checker pins are now labelled per entry and audited by `python3 scripts/pub_arms_index.py --pins`: a pin that resolves under neither convention, or under SHA-1/16 without a labelled SHA-256/16 twin and a naming `hash_note`, fails the check.
